question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and complete the phrase/idiom.

When Jane realised that she had made a serious mistake at work, she knew she had to face the ______and take responsibility for her actions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. music.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "face the music" means to accept the unpleasant consequences of one's own actions; to face criticism or punishment bravely. (अपने कर्मों का परिणाम भुगतना / आलोचना का सामना करना)

◦ Correct: When Jane realised that she had made a serious mistake at work, she knew she had to face the music and take responsibility for her actions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "face the mirror", "face the fun" and "face the band" are not standard English idioms; only "face the music" carries the required meaning of accepting the consequences.

NOTE

• Similar idioms: "bite the bullet" (to face a difficult situation with courage), "pay the piper" (to bear the consequences), "take it on the chin" (to accept misfortune bravely).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Calender.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Calender" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Calendar", meaning a chart showing the days, weeks and months of a year. (कैलेंडर / पंचांग)

◦ Example: Mark the date of the exam on the calendar.

• Spelling key: CAL + EN + DAR — the word ends in "-dar", not "-der".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Conscience" (the inner sense of right and wrong), "Cemetery" (a burial ground — note the three E's) and "Accommodate" (to provide lodging — double C, double M) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Note: "calender" does exist as a rare technical word (a machine for pressing cloth/paper), but for the everyday chart of dates the correct word is "calendar". Frequently confused SSC spellings: cemetery, accommodate, conscience, occasion, committee.

question:
Select the most appropriate word to replace the underlined word in the following sentence.

The officer was polite to the workers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. humble.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Polite" means courteous, well-mannered and respectful. The word closest in sense that can replace it is "humble" — modest, respectful and unassuming. (विनम्र)

◦ Correct: The officer was humble to the workers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "adamant" (stubborn, refusing to change one's mind), Option 2 "officious" (interfering, self-important) and Option 3 "harsh" (cruel, severe) are all opposite or unrelated to "polite".

NOTE

• Synonyms of polite: courteous, humble, civil, gracious, well-mannered. Antonyms: rude, harsh, impolite, insolent. Do not confuse "officious" (bossy/meddlesome) with "official" (relating to an office).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.

A detrimental attitude can always be cured with a cordial approach.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. damaging.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Detrimental" means causing harm or damage; injurious. Its closest synonym is "damaging". (हानिकारक)

◦ Example: Smoking is detrimental/damaging to health.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "unmindful" (careless, not paying attention), Option 2 "social" (relating to society) and Option 4 "cooperative" (willing to help) do not convey the sense of harm.

• "Cordial" in the sentence means warm and friendly. (सौहार्दपूर्ण)

NOTE

• Synonyms of detrimental: damaging, harmful, injurious, deleterious, adverse. Antonyms: beneficial, advantageous, helpful, favourable.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

In accordance to / the factual data, / serious measures are required / to control the loss.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. In accordance to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct fixed expression is "in accordance with" (meaning: in agreement/conformity with), never "in accordance to". So the segment should be "In accordance with".

◦ Correct: In accordance with the factual data, serious measures are required to control the loss.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "the factual data", "serious measures are required" and "to control the loss" are all grammatically correct.

NOTE

• Fixed prepositional phrases often tested in SSC: "in accordance with", "in compliance with", "in conformity with", "in keeping with", but "according to". Never mix them ("according with" and "in accordance to" are both wrong).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Motevate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Motevate" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Motivate", meaning to provide a reason or enthusiasm for doing something; to inspire. (प्रेरित करना)

◦ Example: A good teacher can motivate students to work hard.

• Spelling key: MOTI + VATE — from the noun "motive" (reason), so the second vowel is "i", not "e".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Nostalgia" (a sentimental longing for the past), "Neutral" (not supporting either side) and "Mutual" (shared by two or more parties) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Word family: motive (noun), motivate (verb), motivation (noun), motivated/motivational (adjectives). Related words: nostalgia → nostalgic; neutral → neutrality.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

It is essential that you act in accordance with the rules and regulations of the organisation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. comply.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Comply (with)" means to act in accordance with rules, requests or commands. It is the exact one-word substitute for "act in accordance with". (नियमों का पालन करना)

◦ Correct: It is essential that you comply with the rules and regulations of the organisation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "obey" and 4 "observe" take a direct object (obey the rules / observe the rules) — they do not fit before the preposition "with" that follows in the sentence.

• Option 2 "fulfill" means to complete or satisfy (a promise, a demand) and also does not take "with".

NOTE

• "Comply" is always followed by "with": comply with the rules/orders/instructions. Noun: compliance; adjective: compliant. Antonym: defy, violate, flout.

question:
Select the correct spelling of the underlined word.

"Today's whether is very pleasant", said Maya.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Weather.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence talks about the state of the atmosphere, so the correct word is "weather" — the condition of the atmosphere (sunshine, rain, temperature, etc.) at a place and time. (मौसम)

◦ Correct: "Today's weather is very pleasant", said Maya.

• Spelling key: W + EA + THER.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Wether", "Wheather" and "Weathur" are all incorrect spellings for this meaning.

• The word used in the sentence, "whether", is a conjunction expressing a choice (I don't know whether he will come).

NOTE

• Homophones often tested: weather (मौसम) vs whether (कि/या). Also remember: climate = average weather of a place over a long period; weather = day-to-day condition.

question:
The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment with the grammatical error.

Mahesh and his workers / will have been worked / on the project / for a long time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. will have been worked.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence needs the future perfect continuous tense, whose structure is "will have been + verb-ing". So the correct form is "will have been working", not "will have been worked" (which wrongly uses the past participle).

◦ Correct: Mahesh and his workers will have been working on the project for a long time.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Mahesh and his workers", "on the project" and "for a long time" are all correct.

• The time expression "for a long time" signals a continuing action, confirming the continuous form "working".

NOTE

• Future perfect continuous = will + have + been + V-ing (will have been working/living/studying). Use "for" with a period of time and "since" with a point of time.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

A Gita is considered / to be a dialogue between / the Pandava prince, Arjuna, / and Lord Krishna.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. A Gita is considered.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Names of famous/unique religious books take the definite article "the", not "a". So it must be "The Gita is considered".

◦ Correct: The Gita is considered to be a dialogue between the Pandava prince, Arjuna, and Lord Krishna.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "to be a dialogue between", "the Pandava prince, Arjuna," and "and Lord Krishna" are all correct.

• "A/An" (indefinite articles) are used for non-specific, countable things; "the" is used for things that are one of a kind.

NOTE

• Use "the" before holy books and famous unique works: the Gita, the Ramayana, the Quran, the Bible, the Mahabharata; also before rivers (the Ganga), oceans, newspapers and superlatives.

question: Which of the following sentences contains an error in the use of a phrasal verb?
option_1: Let's call off the picnic as there is a possibility of heavy rain.
option_2: Can you please take care for my belongings for some time?
option_3: It is wise to put up with one's quarrelsome neighbours.
option_4: While visiting the library, I came across an interesting book.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Can you please take care for my belongings for some time?

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrasal expression is "take care of" (to look after), never "take care for". So the sentence should read: Can you please take care of my belongings for some time?

◦ Correct: Please take care of my luggage while I am away.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "call off" = to cancel (call off the picnic) — correct.

• Option 3 "put up with" = to tolerate (put up with quarrelsome neighbours) — correct.

• Option 4 "come across" = to find/meet by chance (came across an interesting book) — correct.

NOTE

• Important phrasal verbs for SSC: call off (cancel), call on (visit), put up with (tolerate), come across (find by chance), look after / take care of (गिरानी करना / देखभाल करना), give up (abandon).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.

If you do not followed the rules, you will not be allowed to stay at this hostel.
option_2: If you do not follow the rules
option_3: If you cannot be following the rules
option_4: If you should not follow the rules
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. If you do not follow the rules.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the auxiliary "do/does/did", the verb must be in the base form (V1). "do not followed" is wrong; it must be "do not follow".

◦ Correct: If you do not follow the rules, you will not be allowed to stay at this hostel.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• This is a first conditional sentence: If + present simple (do not follow), main clause with will (will not be allowed).

• Option 3 "cannot be following" and Option 4 "should not follow" unnecessarily change the structure and meaning.

NOTE

• Rule: do/does/did + base verb (do not follow, does not go, did not come). Conditionals: Type 1 = If + present, ... will + V1; Type 2 = If + past, ... would + V1.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.

After she will get her degree, she moved to Germany.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. After she got her degree.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The main clause is in the past tense ("she moved to Germany"), so the time clause must also be in the past tense: "After she got her degree". A future form ("will get") cannot pair with a past main verb.

◦ Correct: After she got her degree, she moved to Germany.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "After she get" lacks subject–verb agreement (she → gets/got).

• Option 3 "After she gets her degree" (present) would need a present/future main clause (e.g., "she will move"), not "moved".

NOTE

• Sequence of tenses: keep the time clause and main clause in matching time frames. Also, in time clauses beginning with after/when/before/as soon as, do NOT use "will" — use present for future (After she gets her degree, she will move...) or past for past.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.

Mita is smart than many other kids in the school.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. smarter.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" requires the comparative degree. The comparative of "smart" is "smarter".

◦ Correct: Mita is smarter than many other kids in the school.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "most smart" is an incorrect superlative form (the superlative is "smartest" and takes "the", not "than").

• Option 2 "less smart" reverses the intended meaning; Option 3 "smartest" (superlative) cannot be used with "than".

NOTE

• Degrees of comparison: smart – smarter (with "than") – smartest (with "the"). Short adjectives take -er/-est; long adjectives take more/most (more intelligent, most beautiful). Never use double comparatives ("more smarter").

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

The lavish party had a luxurious atmosphere and elegant decorations.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Excessive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lavish" means very elaborate, luxurious and given/spent in great (often excessive) amounts. Its closest synonym here is "excessive" (beyond what is normal). (भव्य / अत्यधिक खर्चीला)

◦ Example: They spent a lavish/excessive amount on the wedding.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Simple" and Option 4 "Middling" (average, mediocre) are near-antonyms of lavish.

• Option 2 "Happy" is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of lavish: extravagant, luxurious, sumptuous, opulent, excessive. Antonyms: simple, frugal, austere, meagre. "Lavish" can also be a verb: to lavish praise on someone (प्रशंसा की बौछार करना).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The billionaire knows how to _____ money.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. make.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct collocation is "make money", meaning to earn money/profit. (पैसा कमाना)

◦ Correct: The billionaire knows how to make money.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "do money", "develop money" and "form money" are not standard English collocations.

• A collocation is a natural pairing of words that native speakers use together.

NOTE

• Common "make/do" collocations for SSC: make money, make a decision, make progress, make an effort, make a mistake; do homework, do a favour, do business, do one's duty.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

By next December / we will has lived / in this city for 28 years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. we will has lived.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the modal "will", the auxiliary must be the base form "have", never "has". The future perfect tense is "will have + V3": "we will have lived".

◦ Correct: By next December we will have lived in this city for 28 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "By next December" and "in this city for 28 years" are correct; the time marker "by + future time" is a classic signal for the future perfect tense.

NOTE

• Modal verbs (will, shall, can, may, must, etc.) are ALWAYS followed by the base form: will have (not "will has"), can go (not "can goes"). Future perfect = will + have + past participle (V3).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.

It is impossible to think of Lady Stranleigh as an ordinary mother.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Usual.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ordinary" means normal, common, with no special features. Its closest synonym is "usual". (साधारण / सामान्य)

◦ Example: It was just an ordinary/usual working day.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Unlucky" (unfortunate) and Option 3 "Blessed" (fortunate/holy) are unrelated.

• Option 2 "Strange" (unusual) is nearly the antonym of ordinary.

NOTE

• Synonyms of ordinary: usual, common, normal, average, commonplace, routine. Antonyms: extraordinary, exceptional, unusual, unique, remarkable.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

Rakesh committed the mistake, and he must be convicted.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Acquitted.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Convicted" means declared guilty of a crime by a court. Its antonym is "acquitted" — declared NOT guilty and set free. (दोषी ठहराया गया का विलोम — बरी किया गया)

◦ Example: He was acquitted because the evidence was insufficient.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Punished" and Option 2 "Sentenced" (given a punishment by a court) are related to conviction, i.e., near-synonyms of the consequence of conviction.

• Option 3 "Crucified" means executed on a cross or, figuratively, severely criticised.

NOTE

• Legal vocabulary for SSC: convict (declare guilty) ↔ acquit (declare not guilty); prosecution ↔ defence; plaintiff ↔ defendant; bail (temporary release); verdict (decision of the court).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

He needs to ___________ as his exams are approaching.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. hit the books.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "hit the books" means to begin studying seriously/hard. It perfectly fits the context of approaching exams. (गंभीरता से पढ़ाई शुरू करना)

◦ Correct: He needs to hit the books as his exams are approaching.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "hit the sack" means to go to bed/sleep.

• Option 2 "bury himself in" is incomplete here (it needs an object — "bury himself in books").

• Option 3 "learn the ropes" means to learn how a particular job/task is done.

NOTE

• "Hit" idioms: hit the books (study hard), hit the sack/hay (go to sleep), hit the road (start a journey), hit the nail on the head (say exactly the right thing), hit the jackpot (have great success).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Credit cards originated in the 1920s in the US, with European references dating back to 1890. John Biggins, 1.______ of the first bank-issued credit card, invented the 'Charge-It' programme in 1946, 2.______ bank customers and local merchants. In 1950, Diners Club introduced their credit card in the US, 3.___________ customers to pay restaurant bills without cash. American Express 4._______ their first credit card in 1958, while the Bank of America introduced the Bank America Card (now Visa) in 1958. Visa, now known as the Visa International Service Association, is accepted in over 150 countries, making it one of the most 5._______ credit cards available.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. inventor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "inventor" is a person who creates something entirely new (a device, a system, a programme). John Biggins created the first bank-issued credit card, so he is called its "inventor" — note the very next clause says he "invented the 'Charge-It' programme". (आविष्कारक)

◦ Correct: John Biggins, inventor of the first bank-issued credit card, invented the 'Charge-It' programme in 1946 ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "producer" (one who manufactures goods or makes films) and Option 2 "finder" (one who finds something lost) do not fit.

• Option 4 "discoverer" is used for finding something that already existed (e.g., Columbus discovered America); a credit card was newly created, not discovered.

NOTE

• Invent = create something new (inventor, invention); discover = find something already existing (discoverer, discovery). This invent/discover distinction is a favourite SSC vocabulary point.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Credit cards originated in the 1920s in the US, with European references dating back to 1890. John Biggins, 1.______ of the first bank-issued credit card, invented the 'Charge-It' programme in 1946, 2.______ bank customers and local merchants. In 1950, Diners Club introduced their credit card in the US, 3.___________ customers to pay restaurant bills without cash. American Express 4._______ their first credit card in 1958, while the Bank of America introduced the Bank America Card (now Visa) in 1958. Visa, now known as the Visa International Service Association, is accepted in over 150 countries, making it one of the most 5._______ credit cards available.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. connecting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Connecting" means joining or linking two parties together. The 'Charge-It' programme linked bank customers with local merchants so payments could flow between them. (जोड़ना)

◦ Correct: ... invented the 'Charge-It' programme in 1946, connecting bank customers and local merchants.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "untangling" (freeing from knots/confusion), Option 3 "smashing" (breaking violently) and Option 4 "splitting" (dividing apart) are all opposite or unrelated to the idea of linking customers with merchants.

NOTE

• Synonyms of connect: link, join, unite, associate, bridge. Antonyms: separate, split, disconnect, divide. The present participle ("connecting") here describes the result of the invention.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Credit cards originated in the 1920s in the US, with European references dating back to 1890. John Biggins, 1.______ of the first bank-issued credit card, invented the 'Charge-It' programme in 1946, 2.______ bank customers and local merchants. In 1950, Diners Club introduced their credit card in the US, 3.___________ customers to pay restaurant bills without cash. American Express 4._______ their first credit card in 1958, while the Bank of America introduced the Bank America Card (now Visa) in 1958. Visa, now known as the Visa International Service Association, is accepted in over 150 countries, making it one of the most 5._______ credit cards available.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. allowing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Allowing" means permitting or enabling someone to do something. The Diners Club card enabled customers to pay restaurant bills without cash. (अनुमति देना / सक्षम बनाना)

◦ Correct: In 1950, Diners Club introduced their credit card in the US, allowing customers to pay restaurant bills without cash.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "prohibiting" and Option 4 "forbidding" mean not permitting — the opposite of what a credit card does.

• Option 2 "enjoying" makes no sense before "customers to pay".

NOTE

• "Allow + object + to + verb" (allowing customers to pay). Synonyms: permit, enable, let (let takes bare infinitive — "let customers pay"). Antonyms: forbid, prohibit, ban.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Credit cards originated in the 1920s in the US, with European references dating back to 1890. John Biggins, 1.______ of the first bank-issued credit card, invented the 'Charge-It' programme in 1946, 2.______ bank customers and local merchants. In 1950, Diners Club introduced their credit card in the US, 3.___________ customers to pay restaurant bills without cash. American Express 4._______ their first credit card in 1958, while the Bank of America introduced the Bank America Card (now Visa) in 1958. Visa, now known as the Visa International Service Association, is accepted in over 150 countries, making it one of the most 5._______ credit cards available.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. issued.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Issued" means officially brought out/distributed for use. Banks and companies "issue" cards, passports, notices and shares — it is the standard collocation for credit cards (the passage itself says "bank-issued credit card"). (जारी किया)

◦ Correct: American Express issued their first credit card in 1958 ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "censored" (officially removed objectionable content) and Option 4 "suppressed" (prevented from being known) are negative and irrelevant.

• Option 3 "published" is used for books, articles and reports, not for cards.

NOTE

• Collocations with "issue": issue a credit/debit card, issue a passport/visa, issue a statement, issue shares. As a noun, "issue" also means a topic or problem.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Credit cards originated in the 1920s in the US, with European references dating back to 1890. John Biggins, 1.______ of the first bank-issued credit card, invented the 'Charge-It' programme in 1946, 2.______ bank customers and local merchants. In 1950, Diners Club introduced their credit card in the US, 3.___________ customers to pay restaurant bills without cash. American Express 4._______ their first credit card in 1958, while the Bank of America introduced the Bank America Card (now Visa) in 1958. Visa, now known as the Visa International Service Association, is accepted in over 150 countries, making it one of the most 5._______ credit cards available.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. universal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Universal" means used or accepted everywhere; applicable to all. As Visa is accepted in over 150 countries, it is "one of the most universal credit cards available". (सार्वभौमिक)

◦ Correct: ... accepted in over 150 countries, making it one of the most universal credit cards available.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• The blank follows "the most" and describes "credit cards", so an adjective is required. Option 2 "solidify" and Option 3 "entitle" are verbs, and Option 4 "amateur" (non-professional) does not fit the sense of worldwide acceptance.

NOTE

• Synonyms of universal: worldwide, global, ubiquitous, widespread. Antonyms: local, limited, restricted. Word forms: universe (noun), universal (adjective), universally (adverb), universality (noun).

question: Identify the INCORRECT pair of cropping season and related crop from the following.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rabi - Paddy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rabi - Paddy" is the incorrect pair. Paddy (rice) is a Kharif crop — it is sown with the onset of the monsoon (June–July) and harvested in September–October, as it needs high temperature and abundant water. (धान — खरीफ फसल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Rabi crops (sown in winter, October–December; harvested in summer, April–June): wheat, barley, gram, peas, mustard.

• Kharif crops (sown with the monsoon; harvested in autumn): paddy (rice), maize, jowar, bajra, cotton, soyabean, groundnut, tur.

• Zaid crops (short summer season between Rabi and Kharif): watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, fodder crops.

NOTE

• "Rabi" and "Kharif" are Arabic words meaning "spring" and "autumn" respectively, referring to the harvest seasons. India is the world's second-largest producer of both rice and wheat.

question: R Muthukannammal, who was awarded the Padma Shri in 2022, is a ______________ dancer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sadir.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• R. Muthukannammal, awarded the Padma Shri in 2022, is a "Sadir" dancer from Viralimalai, Tamil Nadu. She is regarded as one of the last exponents of the devadasi tradition of Sadir dance. (सादिर नृत्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Sadir (also called Sadir Attam or Dasi Attam) is the temple dance tradition of Tamil Nadu performed by devadasis; it is the precursor of Bharatanatyam, which was revived and renamed in the 20th century by reformers like Rukmini Devi Arundale and E. Krishna Iyer.

• Garba is a folk dance of Gujarat; Rouf is a folk dance of Jammu & Kashmir; Chhau is a semi-classical/martial dance of Odisha, Jharkhand and West Bengal.

NOTE

• The Padma Shri is India's fourth-highest civilian award, after the Bharat Ratna, Padma Vibhushan and Padma Bhushan.

question: Calculate the Body Mass Index (BMI) of a person whose weight is 50 kg and height is 1.5 m.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 22.2 kg/m2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Body Mass Index (BMI) = Weight (kg) ÷ [Height (m)]²

◦ BMI = 50 ÷ (1.5)² = 50 ÷ 2.25 = 22.2 kg/m². (बॉडी मास इंडेक्स)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• BMI categories (WHO): below 18.5 — underweight; 18.5–24.9 — normal weight; 25–29.9 — overweight; 30 and above — obese.

• A BMI of 22.2 falls in the normal (healthy) weight range.

NOTE

• BMI is only a screening measure — it does not directly measure body fat. It was devised by the Belgian mathematician Adolphe Quetelet (hence also called the Quetelet index).

question: Which of the following is an Indian folk dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bihu" is a folk dance of Assam, performed during the Bihu festival (especially Rongali/Bohag Bihu in mid-April, the Assamese New Year and harvest festival). It is performed by young men and women to the beats of the dhol and pepa. (बिहू — असम का लोक नृत्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Mohiniyattam (Kerala) and Sattriya (Assam) are all classical dances recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

NOTE

• Famous folk dances: Bihu (Assam), Garba (Gujarat), Bhangra/Giddha (Punjab), Ghoomar (Rajasthan), Lavani (Maharashtra), Rouf (J&K), Yakshagana (Karnataka — folk theatre).

question: Which country won the 4th Asian Kho-Kho Championship 2023 event in the Men's category?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India won the 4th Asian Kho-Kho Championship 2023 in the Men's category (India also won the Women's title). The championship was held at Tamulpur, Assam. (एशियाई खो-खो चैम्पियनशिप 2023 — भारत विजेता)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kho-Kho is a traditional Indian tag sport played between two teams of 12 players (9 on the field), on a rectangular court with two poles.

• The sport is governed in India by the Kho-Kho Federation of India (KKFI); internationally by the International Kho-Kho Federation.

NOTE

• India also won both the Men's and Women's titles at the first Kho Kho World Cup 2025, held in New Delhi. Ultimate Kho Kho is India's franchise-based kho-kho league launched in 2022.

question: The word ‘Megalith’ comes from two ________ words; ‘megas’ means great and ‘lithas’ means stone.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Greek.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Megalith" comes from two Greek words — "megas" meaning great and "lithos/lithas" meaning stone. A megalith is a large stone used to construct a monument or structure. (मेगालिथ — यूनानी शब्द, विशाल पत्थर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Megaliths in India are mostly burial monuments of the Iron Age (c. 1000 BCE onwards), found abundantly in South India (e.g., Brahmagiri, Adichanallur, Hire Benakal) and the Vidarbha region.

• Types of megalithic burials: dolmens, cists, menhirs, cairn circles, urn burials.

• Stonehenge in England is the world's most famous megalithic monument.

NOTE

• Greek roots common in English: "mega" (great — megaphone, megacity), "lith" (stone — Palaeolithic, Neolithic, monolith). Monolith = a structure carved from a single stone (e.g., the rathas of Mahabalipuram).

question: Where was Global Technology Summit 2022 held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is New Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Global Technology Summit (GTS) 2022 — the 7th edition — was held in New Delhi (29 November – 1 December 2022). Its theme was "Geopolitics of Technology". (ग्लोबल टेक्नोलॉजी समिट 2022 — नई दिल्ली)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The summit is co-hosted by the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), Government of India, and Carnegie India.

• It is India's flagship annual event on the intersection of technology, geopolitics and policy, bringing together policymakers, industry experts and academics.

NOTE

• Other major tech events in India: Bengaluru Tech Summit (Karnataka), India Mobile Congress (New Delhi). New Delhi also hosted the G20 Summit 2023.

question: The Ganesh-rath is one of the finest monolithic temples at _____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahabalipuram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Ganesh-rath" is one of the finest monolithic (rock-cut, single-stone) temples at Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram), Tamil Nadu. These rathas were carved under the Pallava dynasty, mainly during the reign of Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla) in the 7th century CE. (गणेश रथ — महाबलीपुरम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Mahabalipuram is famous for the Pancha Rathas (Dharmaraja, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula-Sahadeva and Draupadi rathas), the Shore Temple (built by Narasimhavarman II/Rajasimha) and the giant open-air relief "Descent of the Ganga/Arjuna's Penance".

• The Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1984).

NOTE

• Gangaikondacholapuram was built by the Chola king Rajendra I; Kanchipuram was the Pallava capital; Sarnath (near Varanasi) is where the Buddha delivered his first sermon.

question: Jyotiba Phule belonged from which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jyotiba (Jyotirao) Phule (1827–1890), the great social reformer, belonged to Maharashtra (born in Pune). He fought against caste discrimination and worked for the education of women and the downtrodden. (ज्योतिबा फुले — महाराष्ट्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• In 1848, Jyotiba Phule and his wife Savitribai Phule opened one of India's first schools for girls in Pune; Savitribai is regarded as India's first woman teacher.

• In 1873, he founded the "Satyashodhak Samaj" (Society of Truth Seekers) to secure equal rights for the lower castes.

• His famous book: "Gulamgiri" (Slavery, 1873). He was given the title "Mahatma" in 1888.

NOTE

• Other Maharashtrian reformers: Gopal Hari Deshmukh (Lokahitawadi), M. G. Ranade, Dhondo Keshav Karve and B. R. Ambedkar (who acknowledged Phule as one of his three gurus).

question: On 27th october 2019, Dushyant Chautala took an oath as Deputy Chief Minister of which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Haryana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• On 27 October 2019, Dushyant Chautala, leader of the Jannayak Janta Party (JJP), took oath as the Deputy Chief Minister of Haryana, in the BJP–JJP coalition government headed by Chief Minister Manohar Lal Khattar. (दुष्यंत चौटाला — हरियाणा के उपमुख्यमंत्री)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Dushyant Chautala is the great-grandson of former Deputy Prime Minister Chaudhary Devi Lal; he founded the JJP in 2018 after splitting from the INLD.

• In 2014 he became one of the youngest MPs ever elected to the Lok Sabha (from Hisar).

NOTE

• The post of Deputy Chief Minister is not mentioned in the Constitution; a Deputy CM enjoys the rank of a Cabinet Minister. Haryana was carved out of Punjab on 1 November 1966; its capital is Chandigarh.

question: Where was the Hindu college established in the year 1791 to teach ancient Sanskrit texts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Banaras.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A Sanskrit College (Hindu College) was established at Banaras (Varanasi) in 1791 by Jonathan Duncan, the British Resident, to promote the study of ancient Sanskrit texts, Hindu law and philosophy. (बनारस संस्कृत कॉलेज — 1791, जोनाथन डंकन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Earlier, Warren Hastings had set up the Calcutta Madrasa in 1781 for the study of Muslim law, Arabic and Persian.

• These early institutions reflected the Orientalist policy of the East India Company — promoting traditional Indian learning; later the Anglicists (supported by Macaulay's Minute, 1835) shifted the focus to English education.

NOTE

• The Asiatic Society of Bengal was founded by Sir William Jones in 1784. The Hindu College of Calcutta (1817), associated with Raja Ram Mohan Roy and David Hare, later became Presidency College — do not confuse it with the 1791 Banaras college.

question: Which of the following states of India marked the lowest in National Multi-dimensional Poverty Index: A Progress Review 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the "National Multidimensional Poverty Index: A Progress Review 2023", released by NITI Aayog, Kerala recorded the lowest proportion of multidimensionally poor population (less than 1%) among Indian states. (केरल — सबसे कम बहुआयामी गरीबी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The National MPI measures poverty across three equally weighted dimensions — Health, Education and Standard of Living — using 12 indicators (nutrition, child & adolescent mortality, maternal health, years of schooling, school attendance, cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, assets and bank accounts).

• As per the 2023 review, about 13.5 crore Indians escaped multidimensional poverty between 2015-16 and 2019-21; Bihar had the highest proportion of multidimensionally poor.

NOTE

• The index is based on the global MPI methodology of the UNDP and Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI), using NFHS survey data. Kerala also tops human development indicators like literacy and life expectancy.

question: Which of the following is NOT a part of the capital receipts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tax revenue.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Tax revenue" is a revenue receipt, NOT a capital receipt. Capital receipts are those which either create a liability (e.g., borrowings) or reduce the assets of the government (e.g., disinvestment, recovery of loans). Tax revenue does neither. (कर राजस्व — राजस्व प्राप्ति)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Capital receipts: borrowings (internal and external), recovery of loans given by the government, disinvestment proceeds (sale of PSU shares), small savings.

• Revenue receipts: tax revenue (income tax, GST, corporation tax, customs, excise) and non-tax revenue (interest, dividends and profits, fees, fines, grants).

NOTE

• These classifications appear in the Annual Financial Statement (Union Budget) under Article 112 of the Constitution. Fiscal deficit = total expenditure − total receipts excluding borrowings.

question: On boiling an egg, why does the outer part become opaque and white?
option_1: The heat causes a reaction of the egg with water and makes it opaque.
option_2: The heat causes a change in the crystal structure of egg yolk.
option_3: The heat causes a change in the structure of egg protein.
option_4: The heat causes denaturation, hardening the albumin and colouring it opaque white
solution_text:
The correct answer is The heat causes denaturation, hardening the albumin and colouring it opaque white.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• On boiling an egg, heat causes "denaturation" of the egg white protein (albumin). The protein molecules lose their three-dimensional (globular) structure, unfold and coagulate into a solid network — this hardens the albumin and turns it opaque white. (प्रोटीन का विकृतीकरण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Denaturation is the loss of the secondary and tertiary structure of a protein due to heat, acids, alkalis or alcohol; the primary structure (sequence of amino acids) remains intact. It is generally irreversible for a boiled egg.

• Other everyday examples of denaturation: curdling of milk (lactic acid denatures casein), coagulation of paneer with lemon juice.

NOTE

• Egg white is mainly the protein albumin and water; egg yolk contains fats, proteins and vitamins. Proteins are polymers of amino acids joined by peptide bonds.

question: Which of the following National Parks is located in Madhya Pradesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bandhavgarh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bandhavgarh National Park" is located in the Umaria district of Madhya Pradesh. It is famous for having one of the highest densities of Bengal tigers in the world and was declared a Tiger Reserve in 1993. (बांधवगढ़ राष्ट्रीय उद्यान — मध्य प्रदेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Nanda Devi National Park — Uttarakhand (a UNESCO World Heritage Site, along with the Valley of Flowers).

• Periyar National Park/Tiger Reserve — Kerala (famous for elephants; Periyar lake).

• Silent Valley National Park — Kerala (tropical evergreen forest; lion-tailed macaque).

NOTE

• Madhya Pradesh is called the "Tiger State of India". Its other national parks: Kanha, Pench, Panna, Satpura, Madhav, Sanjay, Van Vihar, Fossil (Dinosaur) National Park, Kuno (home of the reintroduced cheetahs, 2022).

question: Which of the following is the compound with the chemical formula H2SO4?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sulfuric Acid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "H₂SO₄" is the chemical formula of "Sulfuric acid (Sulphuric acid)" — a strong, dibasic mineral acid, often called the "King of Chemicals" or "oil of vitriol". (सल्फ्यूरिक अम्ल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Nitric acid — HNO₃; Sulfurous acid — H₂SO₃; Hydrogen sulfide — H₂S (a gas smelling of rotten eggs).

• Sulfuric acid is manufactured industrially by the Contact Process (catalyst: vanadium pentoxide, V₂O₅).

• Uses: in fertilisers (superphosphate, ammonium sulphate), car batteries (lead-acid), detergents, paints, petroleum refining and as a strong dehydrating agent.

NOTE

• Common acids and formulae for SSC: HCl (hydrochloric), HNO₃ (nitric), H₂SO₄ (sulfuric), H₂CO₃ (carbonic), CH₃COOH (acetic — vinegar), citric acid (lemon), lactic acid (curd).

question: According to Article 74(1), who is at the head of the Council of Ministers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prime Minister.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 74(1) of the Constitution states: "There shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President, who shall act in accordance with such advice." (अनुच्छेद 74(1) — मंत्रिपरिषद का प्रमुख प्रधानमंत्री)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The 42nd Amendment (1976) made the advice of the Council of Ministers binding on the President; the 44th Amendment (1978) allowed the President to send the advice back once for reconsideration.

• Article 75 — the Prime Minister is appointed by the President; other ministers are appointed on the PM's advice; the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (Article 75(3)).

NOTE

• The Prime Minister is described as "primus inter pares" (first among equals). Related articles: Article 74 (Council of Ministers), Article 75 (ministers), Article 78 (PM's duties regarding furnishing information to the President).

question: In which of the following states is the Behdienkhlam Festival celebrated, in which the young men make a symbolic gesture of driving away of the evil spirit, plague and disease by beating the roof of every house with bamboo poles?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meghalaya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Behdienkhlam Festival" is celebrated in Meghalaya, mainly at Jowai in the Jaintia Hills, by the Pnar (Jaintia) tribe. Young men symbolically drive away the evil spirit, plague and disease by beating the roof of every house with bamboo poles. (बेहदीनखलाम — मेघालय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Behdienkhlam" literally means "driving away of the plague/evil" ("khlam" = plague/epidemic). It is celebrated in July after the sowing season, invoking a good harvest.

• The festival is associated with the followers of the indigenous Niamtre faith; a colourful structure called "rath" and decorated "rots" are carried in procession, and men dance in the muddy pool called "Aitnar".

NOTE

• Other festivals of Meghalaya: Shad Suk Mynsiem and Nongkrem dance (Khasi tribe), Wangala (100-drums festival of the Garo tribe). Meghalaya's capital is Shillong; its main tribes are the Khasi, Garo and Jaintia.

question: Who among the following personalities was the recipient of the Lata Mangeshkar Award for Music 2021, presented by the Madhya Pradesh government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kumar Sanu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The renowned playback singer Kumar Sanu received the National Lata Mangeshkar Award for 2021, presented by the Madhya Pradesh government (the award for 2022 went to Shailendra Singh). (लता मंगेशकर पुरस्कार 2021 — कुमार सानू)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The National Lata Mangeshkar Award was instituted by the Madhya Pradesh government in 1984 in honour of the legendary singer Lata Mangeshkar; it is given for excellence in music (playback singing and composition).

• Kumar Sanu is famous for his songs of the 1990s; he won the Filmfare Award for Best Male Playback Singer five consecutive times (1991–95) and received the Padma Shri in 2009.

NOTE

• Lata Mangeshkar (1929–2022), the "Nightingale of India", was honoured with the Bharat Ratna (2001), Padma Bhushan, Padma Vibhushan and the Dadasaheb Phalke Award.

question: The first post-independence National Games were hosted by which of the following cities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lucknow.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first National Games after independence were hosted by Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh) in 1948. (स्वतंत्रता के बाद प्रथम राष्ट्रीय खेल — लखनऊ, 1948)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The National Games began as the Indian Olympic Games, first held at Lahore in 1924; they were renamed the National Games in 1940 (Bombay).

• The Games are organised under the aegis of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) to promote Olympic sports in the country.

• Recent editions: 2022 — Gujarat, 2023 — Goa (37th), 2025 — Uttarakhand (38th).

NOTE

• The Indian Olympic Association was founded in 1927; its first president was Sir Dorabji Tata. The National Games are held on the pattern of the Olympics, with states and UTs competing.

question: The Hindu temples ‘Hinglaj Mata’ and ‘Katasraj’ are located in which neighbouring country of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pakistan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Hindu temples "Hinglaj Mata" and "Katasraj" are located in Pakistan. (हिंगलाज माता और कटासराज मंदिर — पाकिस्तान)

◦ Hinglaj Mata temple — in the Hingol National Park, Balochistan province; it is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas and the site of the annual Hinglaj Yatra.

◦ Katasraj temple complex — in the Chakwal district of Punjab province, dedicated mainly to Lord Shiva; its sacred pond is believed to have been formed from Shiva's tears.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Katasraj site is also associated with the Pandavas, who are said to have spent part of their exile there (linked to the Yaksha-Yudhishthira dialogue).

• Another famous Hindu shrine in Pakistan is the Shri Ramdev Pir temple and the Panchmukhi Hanuman temple (Karachi).

NOTE

• India shares land borders with Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and Myanmar; Sri Lanka is separated by the Palk Strait.

question: The officer known as Diwan belonged to which of the following departments of the Mughal empire during Akbar’s reign?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Finance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• During Akbar's reign, the officer known as the "Diwan (Diwan-i-Kul / Wazir)" headed the Finance (revenue) department of the Mughal empire. He supervised the income and expenditure of the state and the land-revenue administration. (दीवान — वित्त/राजस्व विभाग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other key Mughal officers: Mir Bakhshi — head of the military department (pay and muster of soldiers, mansabdars); Mir Saman/Khan-i-Saman — royal household and karkhanas; Sadr-us-Sudur — religious grants and charity; Qazi-ul-Quzat — chief judge (judicial department).

• Raja Todar Mal, Akbar's famous Diwan, introduced the standard land-revenue system called the Dahsala (Zabti) system and was one of Akbar's Navratnas.

NOTE

• Akbar's mansabdari system ranked officers by "zat" and "sawar". Under the treaty of Allahabad (1765), the East India Company obtained the Diwani (revenue rights) of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa — the same word "diwan" in use.

question: Which of the following Articles on Fundamental Duties was added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 51-A.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution as Article 51-A (in a new Part IV-A) by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee. (अनुच्छेद 51-क — मौलिक कर्तव्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Originally 10 Fundamental Duties were added; the 11th duty (parents/guardians to provide education to children aged 6–14) was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

• The Fundamental Duties are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR; they are non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts).

• Examples: to abide by the Constitution, respect the National Flag and Anthem, protect the environment, develop scientific temper, safeguard public property.

NOTE

• Article 40 — organisation of village panchayats (a Directive Principle). The 42nd Amendment (1976) is called the "Mini-Constitution"; it also added the words "socialist", "secular" and "integrity" to the Preamble.

question: The famous Hindi novel ‘Maila Aanchal’ is written by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Phanishwar Nath Renu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous Hindi novel "Maila Aanchal" (1954) was written by Phanishwar Nath 'Renu'. It is regarded as the most celebrated "aanchalik (regional) upanyas" in Hindi, depicting the life of a village in the Purnea region of Bihar around independence. (मैला आँचल — फणीश्वरनाथ रेणु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Renu's other works: "Parti Parikatha", and the story "Maare Gaye Gulfam", on which the film "Teesri Kasam" was based. He was honoured with the Padma Shri.

• Shrilal Shukla wrote the satirical classic "Raag Darbari"; Premchand wrote "Godaan", "Gaban", "Nirmala"; Mridula Garg wrote "Chittacobra", "Kathgulab".

NOTE

• "Maila Aanchal" is considered second only to Premchand's "Godaan" in the tradition of the Hindi rural novel, and it established the "aanchalik" (regionalist) genre in Hindi literature.

question: The average separation between the sun and the earth in terms of light years is 8.311 minutes. Here, minutes indicate:
solution_text:
The correct answer is distance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When the Sun–Earth separation is expressed as "8.311 (light) minutes", the "minutes" here indicate distance, not time. A "light minute" is the distance travelled by light in one minute; similarly a light year is the distance travelled by light in one year. (यहाँ मिनट दूरी का सूचक है)

◦ Distance = speed of light × time = 3 × 10⁸ m/s × 60 s ≈ 1.8 × 10¹⁰ m per light minute.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Sunlight takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach the Earth; the average Sun–Earth distance is about 1.496 × 10¹¹ m = 1 Astronomical Unit (AU).

• 1 light year ≈ 9.46 × 10¹⁵ m; other distance units in astronomy: the astronomical unit (AU) and the parsec (≈ 3.26 light years).

NOTE

• Despite containing the word "year/minute", light year and light minute are units of DISTANCE — a classic SSC trick question. The nearest star after the Sun, Proxima Centauri, is about 4.24 light years away.
